claim:
Let \(\Sigma\) be an alphabet of size \(q\ge 2\), let \(k\ge 1\), and let \(n\ge q\). For a full-support word \(w\in\Sigma^n\), let \(I_k(w)\) be the minimum number of symbol insertions needed to obtain a word containing every length-\(k\) word over \(\Sigma\) as a subsequence. Then the exact worst-case insertion distance on the full-support layer is
\[
R_q(n,k):=\max_{\substack{w\in\Sigma^n\\\operatorname{alph}(w)=\Sigma}} I_k(w)
=\max\{qk-n,(q-1)(k-1)\}.
\]
Equivalently, the two regimes meet at \(n=q+k-1\): the radius is \(qk-n\) for \(q\le n\le q+k-1\), and \((q-1)(k-1)\) for \(n\ge q+k-1\). For any ordering \(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{q-1}\) of \(\Sigma\), the word \(a_0^{\,n-q+1}a_1a_2\cdots a_{q-1}\) attains the maximum.
integrity: The theorem is stated only at the strength proved. The earliest public source date is taken from the first arXiv posting. Prior algorithms for per-word insertion distance are credited and are not presented as new.
scientific_limitations: Insertion distance only; the starting word must have full support on the fixed ambient alphabet. The result gives the worst-case value and one extremal family, not a classification of all maximizers. Finite verification supports but does not replace the all-parameter proof.
title: Exact full-support insertion radius of subsequence universality
